headline: Quantum Dynamics: From Particle Tracks to Dissipation
summary: Today's research spans distinct quantum domains, highlighting new advances in quantum kernel classification for particle physics, Lie-type decompositions for open Markovian systems, and heavy Fermi polaron experiments. Each paper showcases the ongoing transition of quantum methods into rigorous application and complex system modeling.

themes.title: Quantum Machine Learning in High-Energy Physics
themes.body: A scalable quantum kernel classification workflow was designed for particle-track events. Utilizing a 6-qubit state via a ZZFeatureMap, the ideal quantum support vector classifier achieved 99.99% recall on 500,000 track events.

themes.title: Structural Geometry of Open Quantum Systems
themes.body: Researchers proved a Levi-type decomposition theorem for dynamical Lie wedges in Markovian quantum dynamics, demonstrating that total dissipation strength is determined solely by the solvable radical coordinate.

themes.title: Experimental Fermi Polaron Platforms
themes.body: A new experimental platform successfully immersed 1,000 cesium impurities into a degenerate Fermi gas of 200,000 lithium atoms, using Raman spectroscopy to explore regimes enabled by large mass imbalances.
